heading: Kaitiaki
opening: A digital safe with more than one key, held by people you trust.
summary_1: Kaitiaki encrypts your files and splits the key among people you choose, with Shamir's Secret Sharing. You set how many of them must come together to recover the files. Two of three, three of five, whatever fits. No single guardian can open anything alone.
summary_2: Each guardian gets a bundle with everything they need to recover. Recovery is opening a file in a browser, offline*, with no accounts and no servers. If this website disappears, recovery still works.
bg_1: Two things led me to build Kaitiaki.
bg_2: Kaitiaki is the Bitcoin Butlers fork of Rememory by eljojo. Kaitiaki is the te reo Māori word for a guardian. We use the tool for the records a multisig wallet needs beside its seeds. Those records are the wallet descriptor, the cosigner public keys and the instructions your family will need one day.
bg_3: The tool is free, forever, and it runs on your own computer. The service is the practice. A Butler guides your placement session over video, and an annual drill rehearses the recovery with your guardians. We see screens, never bytes, and we never hold a bundle.
bg_4: Seed words never go in a bundle. Seeds belong on steel or in a codex32 kit. Read about the placement session.
bg_changelog: Kaitiaki keeps growing. Check the changelog to see what's new.
how_subtitle: You choose who to trust and how many must agree. Your files are encrypted, the key is split into pieces, and each person keeps one. When enough of them come together, the files are unlocked.
how_caption: Any three of five can recover the files
how_fallback:
Your File → Encrypt → Split key into 5 pieces → Distribute to guardians
↓
Any 3 guardians → Combine pieces → Unlock → File recovered
bundles_desc: Each guardian receives a self-contained bundle. It is a ZIP file with a recovery tool that works in any browser, offline, with no installation. If this project disappears, recovery still works.
bundles_contacts: Every bundle includes contact details for the other guardians, so they can coordinate without you.
trust_1: Recovery works without this project existing. Each bundle is self-contained
trust_2: The code is open source. Read it on GitHub
trust_3: A security self-review explains the cryptographic choices
trust_4: Everything runs locally. Your files never leave your device
trust_5: Try the demo bundles before using it with anything important
trust_6: Encryption uses age, a modern and well-regarded tool
trust_7: Read more about what protects your data and what could go wrong
try_step_1: Open Create bundles and add two or three guardians with made-up names.
try_step_2: Add one harmless file, then generate and download the bundles.
try_step_3: Unzip one bundle and open its recover.html in your browser.
try_step_4: Drag the README.txt files from the other bundles onto the page. When enough pieces are in, the file unlocks.
try_note: This is what a real recovery feels like. Do it once with a test file before you trust the tool with anything important.
whatis_is_1: A free tool that runs in your browser, offline*
whatis_is_2: A way to split the key to your backup among people you trust
whatis_is_4: Self-contained. Recovery works without this website
whatis_isnt_1: A custodian. We never hold a bundle, a share or your files
whatis_isnt_2: An account or a cloud product
whatis_isnt_4: A backup on its own. Media rots and people move. Drill it every year
footer_timelock: * Time-locked archives need a brief internet connection at recovery time.
